The story is written in the format of a script, relying almost entirely on dialogue and minimal stage directions. Beyond noting that the café is "dimly lit" (sight) and that Lukas speaks "quietly" (sound), the writer does not include sensory details. There are no descriptions of the smells of the café, the ambient sounds, the textures or temperatures of the objects (like the coffee cup or the spoon), or the tastes of the drinks (in fact, the coffee remains untouched). Because it lacks descriptions that appeal to the five senses, the environment does not feel tangible or rich at a sensory level.
